correctness.rationale: Every eigenscalar of the sketched Ritz matrix is u*T A u/(u*T u), with positive real denominator. The squared-norm embedding gives a Hermitian compression H of T-I with ||H||<=epsilon on span(u,Au). The exact support function of u*H Au is epsilon sqrt(a^2 cos^2(phi)+b^2), hence the possible numerator is a translated ellipse; the tangent halfplane inequality gives sin(angle)=epsilon b/[a sqrt(1-epsilon^2)]. The positive polynomial (A-mu I)(L I-A) bounds b/a sharply by (L-mu)/(2sqrt(mu L)); this yields the stated angle and strict distortion threshold. A two-mode complex Gram sketch realizes tangency, the algebraic kappa=9 case reproduces lambda=(5+sqrt(2)i)/3, and real Gram matrices with off-diagonal -epsilon realize zero/negative Ritz values at/above the critical distortion. Packaged verify.py passed exact rational checks and 8,750 random complex embedding cases. Finite tests are not the proof.

value.rationale: The sRR eigenproblem for Hermitian A is generally nonsymmetric and can create nonreal eigenvalues. The new law completely solves a natural worst-case quantitative spectral-location question: it gives a sharp, dimension-independent distortion-to-angle conversion and a critical point of loss of positive-real location, with a genuine dimension-reducing witness. The result applies to every trial-space dimension under the exact joint-space embedding and can inform deterministic embedding design. It does not rely merely on naming a classical inequality; the matrix-pencil-specific sharp ellipse geometry and equality example provide an intrinsic numerical-analysis conclusion. It neither assumes nor claims sketch probability distributions, finite-precision stability, or convergence of complete algorithms.
